description: The procedure for laying out and tooling a title on a spine for extra binding: building a folded lettering paper, centring each line, transferring guide lines to the panel, then gilding and striking the letters outward from the centre.
name: lettering the back

source_ref.label: Douglas Cockerell, Bookbinding and the Care of Books (1901), Chapter XV, p.215. Internet Archive.
Douglas Cockerell, Bookbinding and the Care of Books (D. Appleton, 1901), Internet Archive

steps.description: Cut a strip of thin paper as wide as the height of the panel and fold it to establish a centred line square to the head and tail.
Fold to the width of the back and fold again at the exact centre so the strip carries reference folds for the panel.
Select a letter size, mark a trial row of the same letter, and lay the folded paper against it to judge how many letters fit per line.
Break the title into lines that fit, choosing a smaller letter rather than splitting an awkward word, and avoid mixing letter designs.
Set the line positions by stepping off equal spaces with dividers through the folded paper, then join the points against a straight-edge to raise guide lines.
Find the centre letter of each line, counting word spaces as letters, and mark it first so the others can be added evenly on each side.
Glaire the panel, lay the gold, and strike the letters working outward from the centre to the prepared guide lines.
